text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) rated Hungarian chemicals maker Borsodchem Rt's shares as "buy", saying that the appearently weak results were still in line with expectations.
"These results, although on face value they seem weak, are in line with our expectations," CFSB's Budapest-based analyst Spencer Jakab said in a compnay update on Tuesday.
Earlier today Borsodchem reported a January-September group net profit of 4.41 billion forints, down from 4.93 billion in the same period of 1995.
The main reasons for CSFB's rating were Borsodchem's capacity increases, the analyst said.

The company has increased its methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) -- its most profitable product -- capacity to 32,500 tonnes per year from 25,000 tonnes, but as the plant on came on line on September 26, this is not reflected in the results just released.
Furthermore, PVC capacity has also been raised to 250,000 tonnes per year from 210,000 tonnes and this increase also results in lower costs even if not running at full capacity.
"The older and much less efficient PVC 1 facility will become a 'swing plant' with lower utilisation when demand is lower," Jakab said.
"The yearly maintenance of the chloralkali plant traditionally makes the third quarter weaker than any other quarter," he said.
PVC prices rose 13 to 14 percent in the third quarter, while primary input material costs only rose by six percent, widening Borsodchem's margin.
Although Borsodchem stocks have realised much of their original growth potenital, the report said "we see moderate appreciation potential of 15 to 20 percent... on a four to six months view."
Borsodchem shares closed at 3,310 forints, down 35.
